column4: Make names the makefile line, the target and the recipe's status in one line; Ronin reports a failure Ninja's way.
Ronin prints Ninja's [N/M] progress line where Make echoes the recipe.
Make echoes the recipe line it is about to run; Ronin prints a progress line instead. Recognised by reading the makefile the case ran, not by guessing.
Ronin reports a failed command with Ninja's FAILED: block and its own stopped line.
the diagnostic is Ronin's by name, where the suite expects the name it probed for.
the two tools bracket a -C build with Entering and Leaving at different moments.
Ronin says it had nothing to do; Make says nothing at all.
the same lines in a different order: Make interleaves each recipe line with the output of running it, and Ronin runs the recipe as one script.
Ronin refused an option the test passed and GNU Make accepted.
the evaluator says outright that it does not support a construct the makefile used; .SECONDEXPANSION is most of it.
Ronin cannot find a rule for a target GNU Make built, so a rule that should have matched did not: an implicit rule, a vpath search, or a suffix rule.
both tools refused to build the same target for the same reason and worded it differently.
both tools refused, naming a different link of the same broken chain: Make walks further in before giving up.
Ronin found no makefile to read where GNU Make found one.
both tools refused for the same reason and worded it differently; ours carries Rust's "(os error N)" suffix.
a makefile read MAKEFLAGS and got a different set of switches from the one GNU Make puts there.
Ronin could not parse a makefile GNU Make read: missing separator is most of it.
the Makefile evaluated to something else, or the build did something else: a different value, a different rule, a different file, a different status.
